nyciml-2024-25-spring-junior-01.prompt: Suppose $2025$ people are in a row. The first person says “at most $1$ of us is lying,” the second says “at most $2$ of us are lying,” and so on, until the $2025$th person says “at most $2025$ of us are lying.” How many people are lying?

nyciml-2024-25-spring-junior-02.prompt: In a plane, Bob draws two rays that both originate at point $A$. Every second, he draws another ray from point $A$ to bisect an acute angle formed by two existing rays, until he can no longer do so. Including the original two rays, what is the maximum number of rays Bob can draw in this way, such that the angle between any two rays is a positive integer number of degrees?

nyciml-2024-25-spring-junior-03.prompt: How many unordered pairs of integers from $1$ to $99$ (inclusive) have one integer containing the other? For example, $122$ contains the integers $1$, $2$, $12$, $22$, and $122$.
nyciml-2024-25-spring-junior-03.reviewNote: Official answer 261 counts the 99 pairs of a number with itself (the example says 122 contains 122). Reading 'pairs' as two different integers gives 162, also accepted.

nyciml-2024-25-spring-junior-04.prompt: Given a regular hexagon with center $C$, consider the shape represented by the set of all points closer to $C$ than to any vertex of the hexagon. What is the ratio of the area of this shape to the area of the regular hexagon?

nyciml-2024-25-spring-junior-06.prompt: Adam has a square birthday cake, with side length $8$, and he wants to slice it. Every cut he makes must go all the way from one side to the cake to the other, parallel to an edge. Given that, by the end, every piece must be of size $1\times1$, $1\times2$, $2\times1$, or $2\times2$, how many ways are there for Adam to slice his cake without considering the order of the cuts?

nyciml-2024-25-spring-junior-07.prompt: Frank and Aaron are eating cookies from the IML factory. They are splitting $6$ cookies evenly, and start eating at the same time. After $8$ minutes Aaron finishes his share of cookies as Frank finishes two cookies. How much longer will it take for Frank to finish his share of cookies, in seconds?

nyciml-2024-25-spring-junior-08.prompt: Let $s(n)$ be the sum of the digits of $n$, and $r(n)$ be the number obtained when the digits of $n$ are reversed. For example, $s(52)=7$ and $r(52)=25$. If $s(x)=s(x+r(x))$ and $x$ has $2$ nonzero digits, find the minimum possible value of $x$.

nyciml-2024-25-spring-junior-09.prompt: Let $p$ and $q$ be primes such that $p^2+q^2$ is also prime. Find the maximum possible value of $10pq-p^2-q^2$.

nyciml-2024-25-spring-junior-10.prompt: $\triangle ABC$ has $AB=AC=10$, and $BC=12$. Let $D$ be the foot of the altitude from $C$ to $AB$, and let $E$ be the midpoint of $CD$. Find $BE^2$.

nyciml-2024-25-spring-junior-11.prompt: Suppose $a^b=2\cdot4\cdot8\cdot16\cdot32$. If $a$ and $b$ are both integers greater than $1$, find the sum of all possible values of $a$.

nyciml-2024-25-spring-junior-12.prompt: Let $P$ be the product of all the factors of $15000$. How many zeroes are at the end of $P$?

nyciml-2024-25-spring-junior-13.prompt: You roll a fair standard $8$-sided dice twice. Find the probability that the product of the rolls is a multiple of $4$.

nyciml-2024-25-spring-junior-14.prompt: Each square in a $45\times45$ grid contains an integer. The bottom left square has the integer $0$, and every integer is strictly greater than the integer directly below it (unless it is in the bottom row) and the integer directly to its left (unless it is in the left column). You pick $45$ integers, all in different rows and columns. What is their minimum possible sum?

nyciml-2024-25-spring-junior-15.prompt: How many squares of any size are contained in an $8\times8$ chessboard that have the same number of white and black squares?

nyciml-2024-25-spring-junior-16.prompt: Find all integer solutions to $x^3+2x^2y+2xy^2+y^3=3$. Write your answer as a set of ordered pairs of the form $(x,y)$.

nyciml-2024-25-spring-junior-17.prompt: $\triangle ABC$ has $AB=AC$. Let $D$, $E$ be points on $\overline{AB}$, $\overline{AC}$ respectively such that $\angle ADC=\angle AED$. Given that $AE=4$ and $EC=5$, find $BD$.

nyciml-2024-25-spring-junior-18.prompt: An odd positive integer is written on a chalkboard. Each minute, if an odd integer $n$ is on the board, Alice replaces it with $\frac{3n+1}2$. She stops when she writes an even integer $x$. Given that $x+1$ has $3$ distinct prime factors and $360$ total factors, find the greatest possible number of integers Alice could have written on the board (not including the original number, but including the final even number).
